blocks.orig: We love Africa – its animals, its nature and its people. That’s why we want to protect this wonderful continent by all means. At the same time, we want as many people as possible to see the wonders of Tanzania with their own eyes. So let’s be clear: responsible tourism is very important to us.
blocks.html: Africa has our hearts: the animals, the nature, the people. That is exactly why we want to do everything we can to protect this wonderful continent, while also wanting as many people as possible to witness the wonders of Tanzania for themselves. So let there be no doubt: responsible tourism matters a great deal to us.

blocks.orig: If you now think, “well that’s all very nice, but how can ‘responsible’ and ‘tourism’ go together?” we can’t blame you. Obviously, the tourism industry isn’t the most eco-friendly sector. But we’re doing our best to give something back to the planet and the people while offering unforgettable journeys. We’re definitely not perfect, but we’re constantly looking for ways to do better.
blocks.html: Perhaps you are thinking, “that sounds lovely, but how do ‘responsible’ and ‘tourism’ fit together?” and we understand the question. The tourism industry is clearly not the greenest sector around. Still, we do our utmost to give something back to the planet and its people while creating unforgettable trips. We are far from perfect, but we never stop searching for ways to improve.

blocks.orig: In this article we want to have a look at disadvantages and advantages of tourism, what we are currently doing to protect the nature and support the locals and what you can do yourself.
blocks.html: In this article we look at the downsides and the upsides of tourism, at what we are doing right now to protect nature and support local people, and at what you can do yourself.

blocks.orig: Okay, let’s crack on then, shall we?
blocks.html: Right then, shall we get started?

blocks.orig: Let’s start with the biggest disadvantage of tourism on the environment, which is a no-brainer: flying. In order to get places, you have to use a means of transport. And while you can use public transport for a trip within your country or even your continent, going to Tanzania only leaves you with one option (unless you have a lot of time and crave an adventure on another level).
blocks.html: We begin with the most obvious drawback tourism has for the environment: flying. To get anywhere you need some form of transport, and while public transport will do for a journey within your own country or even your continent, a trip to Tanzania really leaves just one option (unless you have plenty of time and are after an adventure of a whole different kind).

blocks.orig: Also, the more people travel to a country, the bigger is the toll on the country. Agricultural space and landscapes need to make space for roads and hotels, more people mean more emissions and waste and some ancient cultural traditions might get lost. And thanks to Instagram, hidden gems tend to turn into highly sought-after safari hotspots, disturbing animals and nature alike.
blocks.html: On top of that, the more visitors a country receives, the heavier the burden it carries. Farmland and landscapes give way to roads and hotels, more people bring more emissions and more waste, and some age-old cultural traditions risk disappearing. And thanks to Instagram, quiet hidden gems turn into sought-after safari hotspots, unsettling wildlife and nature alike.

blocks.orig: However, tourism also has its advantages and with that we leave this article’s gloomy side and start painting a brighter picture in the next part.
blocks.html: Tourism does bring benefits too, though, and with that we leave the gloomy part of this article behind and move on to a brighter picture.

blocks.orig: If we talk about which advantages tourism can have for a country and its people, we best ask a local. Like our director, our team in Arusha Mndevu, who grew up in Lushoto in the Usambara Mountains and has been in the tourism industry since 1996.
blocks.html: Who better to ask about the benefits tourism brings to a country and its people than someone who lives there? Our director, our team in Arusha Mndevu, for instance, who grew up in Lushoto in the Usambara Mountains and has worked in tourism since 1996.

blocks.orig: The tourism sector doesn’t only provide him with a job he’s passionate about, but also with a steady income. This means he can support his family as well as shops and restaurants in his community. A virtuous circle, if you want.
blocks.html: Tourism gives him not just a job he loves but a reliable income too, which lets him provide for his family and spend money at the shops and restaurants in his community. Call it a virtuous circle.

blocks.orig: The advantages, however, can also be seen on a larger scale. More people travelling to a country also mean more money for the country – something especially developing countries heavily rely on. Having more funds at their disposal, they can support their people and use it for conservation purposes or landscape conservancy. So yes, travelling harms the planet, but it also does good.
blocks.html: The benefits show up on a bigger scale as well. More visitors to a country mean more money flowing in, something developing countries in particular depend on heavily. With more funds available, a country can look after its people and invest in conservation or protecting its landscapes. So yes, travel does harm the planet, but it also does a lot of good.

blocks.orig: Our commitments to encourage responsible tourism in Tanzania
blocks.html: What we commit to for responsible tourism in Tanzania

blocks.orig: The well-being of animals, people, and landscapes is our top-priority, no matter what we do. This means, for example, that we get close to your favourite animals during a safari, but thanks to our guides’ extensive knowledge we never disturb them.
blocks.html: Whatever we do, the welfare of animals, people and landscapes comes first. On safari, for instance, we bring you close to the animals you most want to see, but our guides know so much about them that we never disturb them.

blocks.orig: Of course, we also want to make sure that you travel as safely and eco-friendly as possible when travelling with us. That’s why we’ve taken some matters into our own hands – from hospitality training and educational programmes to local recycling initiatives and green energy consumption.
blocks.html: Naturally, we also want your travels with us to be as safe and as environmentally friendly as they can be. That is why we have taken a number of things into our own hands, from hospitality training and educational programmes to local recycling schemes and the use of green energy.

blocks.orig: When picking our accommodation partners, we of course check for comfiness and authenticity. But we also have a list of environmental criteria we want to have fulfilled: from waste reduction to green energy. And since the sun watches over Tanzania most of the time, it powers 75% of our accommodation options via solar panels.
blocks.html: When we choose accommodation partners, comfort and authenticity are of course on the checklist. But we also apply a set of environmental criteria, ranging from waste reduction to green energy. And because the sun shines over Tanzania most of the time, solar panels supply the power at 75% of the places we offer.

blocks.orig: Of course, you can enjoy a safari in our 4x4s. We regularly update our fleet with a focus on an innovative and sustainable performance. However, if you only want to only leave your real footprints behind, you can join a hiking adventure, a biking tour, a canoeing safari or sleep in a simple tent under the stars.
blocks.html: You are welcome, of course, to go on safari in one of our 4x4s; we renew our fleet regularly with innovation and sustainable performance in mind. But if you prefer to leave nothing but your own footprints, you can opt for a hiking adventure, a cycling tour, a canoe safari or a night in a simple tent beneath the stars.

blocks.orig: In 2020, we launched our Manyara Tree Planting Project close to Arusha National Park. The initial 30 acres have quickly grown to 48 acres, and we’re far from stopping. By planting more indigenous trees, we want to capture at least some of our industry’s emissions.
blocks.html: Our Manyara Tree Planting Project near Arusha National Park started in 2020. What began as 30 acres has quickly expanded to 48 acres, and we have no intention of stopping. By planting more native trees we aim to offset at least part of our industry's emissions.

blocks.orig: When our team in Arusha was 16 years old, he suffered from a strong flu, leaving him unconscious. The catholic sisters of the Gare Catholic Dispensary took care of him and since we are extremely thankful for that, we wanted to support this life-saving institution. We donated medicines, mattresses, bedsheets, and hope to soon be able to give them an ultrasound and an X-ray machine.
blocks.html: At the age of 16, our team in Arusha came down with a severe bout of flu that left him unconscious. The Catholic sisters of the Gare Catholic Dispensary nursed him back to health, and out of deep gratitude we wanted to give something back to this life-saving institution. We have donated medicines, mattresses and bedsheets, and hope to provide an ultrasound and an X-ray machine before long.

blocks.orig: The founders of Your Tanzania Trip wanted to recognise Tanzanian tourism businesses operating with nature in mind, which is why they launched this initiative. If they operate with the environment as their priority, stick to sustainable practices and play their role in our commitment to creating a sustainable Tanzania for all, they can adorn themselves with this prestigious title.
blocks.html: This initiative was launched by the founders of Your Tanzania Trip to give recognition to Tanzanian tourism businesses that work with nature in mind. Businesses that put the environment first, follow sustainable practices and do their part in our shared commitment to a sustainable Tanzania for everyone may carry this prestigious title.

blocks.orig: Nothing would be possible without are employees. From our office staff to our guides in the bush – they all undergo a lengthy selection process and in-depth training, including environmental awareness.
blocks.html: None of this would be possible without our employees. Everyone, from office staff to the guides out in the bush, goes through a thorough selection process and in-depth training, environmental awareness included.

blocks.orig: Youth unemployment is a big issue in Tanzania. In order to give kids and young adults a future, we have set up the Hakuna Matata Academy in 2022, where we train around 200 street kids per year. The focus lies on basic life skills, but also on knowledge about wildlife, nature, and the hospitality sector. Our goal: we want to offer and get them trainings in this industry. The more they know, the better can they protect nature and support their community.
blocks.html: Youth unemployment is a serious problem in Tanzania. To give children and young adults a future, we founded the Hakuna Matata Academy in 2022, where around 200 street kids receive training every year. The emphasis is on basic life skills, but also on knowledge of wildlife, nature and the hospitality sector. Our aim is to offer them training in this industry and to help them find it. The more they know, the better they can look after nature and support their community.

blocks.orig: As you can see, we don’t just say that responsible tourism is important to us. We don’t shy away from taking responsibility for Tanzania’s nature, animals, and people. Of course, there’s always room for improvement, which is why we constantly look for more possibilities.
blocks.html: So responsible tourism is not just something we talk about. We are not afraid to take responsibility for the nature, animals and people of Tanzania. There is always more to be done, of course, which is why we keep looking for new possibilities.

blocks.orig: No matter if you travel to Tanzania or another country – you can always play your role in the sustainability picture.
blocks.html: Whether you are heading to Tanzania or somewhere else entirely, you can always do your bit for sustainability.

blocks.orig: We have put together eight valuable tips applicable to anywhere and anytime.
blocks.html: Here are eight useful tips that work anywhere, at any time.

blocks.orig: When booking your flight, tick the little box saying “carbon compensation”.
blocks.html: Tick the small “carbon compensation” box when you book your flight.

blocks.orig: Support local businesses and respect cultures and customs.
blocks.html: Back local businesses and respect local cultures and customs.

blocks.orig: Choose eco-friendly options when possible, e.g. take the train to your local airport.
blocks.html: Go for the eco-friendly choice whenever you can, such as taking the train to your local airport.

blocks.orig: Respect nature and wildlife: take your rubbish with you and observe animals from a distance – do not feed them.
blocks.html: Show respect for nature and wildlife: carry your rubbish out with you, watch animals from a distance and never feed them.

blocks.orig: Take part in responsible activities like nature walks, biking tours or a canoe safari.
blocks.html: Join responsible activities such as nature walks, cycling tours or a canoe safari.

blocks.orig: Check for any country- or activity-specific guidelines regarding responsible tourism and stick to them.
blocks.html: Look up any guidelines on responsible tourism that apply to the country or activity, and follow them.

blocks.orig: Support conservation efforts with donations – a few dollars can go a long way.
blocks.html: Back conservation work with a donation – even a few dollars can make a real difference.

blocks.html: Turn your phone off: the good old internet is responsible for a lot of CO<sup>2</sup><sup> </sup>emissions, and although this tip won't change the world, every little helps, and it gives you that ultimate sense of holiday freedom!
